messages.subject: qqnorm and ggplot2 (second round)
parts:
Hi,

After reading this qqnorm and ggplot2 post (http://groups.google.com/
group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/e0dc61c51b1e992e), I was wondering
how to specify custom quantile in stat_qq. Any suggestion welcome!

Thank you in advance,

Thomas



On Jan 11, 4:59 pm, hadley wickham <h.wick...@gmail.com> wrote:
is what base-R does, not what ggplot actually does. It might be that
ggplot is right, I am not knowledgeable enough to know that, but I
think it should be justified on the help page of stat_qq, with an
appropriate reference. And, at least because it is different from the
default behaviour of R (however wrong it may be), it should be
strongly argumented.

Ok, I finally get what you're complaining about and I think you're
right - I was using the quantiles for both the sample and theoretical
distributions, when I should only be using them for the theoretical.

Here's what the new code will look like:

data <- remove_missing(data, na.rm, "sample", name = "stat_qq")

sample <- sort(data$sample)
n <- length(sample)

# Compute theoretical quantiles
if (is.null(quantiles)) {
quantiles <- ppoints(n)
} else {
stopifnot(length(quantiles) == n)
}
theoretical <- safe.call(distribution, list(p = quantiles, ...))

data.frame(sample, theoretical)

But that means you can no longer specify (e.g.) quantiles = seq(0.05,
0.95, by = 0.05)) if you have a large dataset and only want to see
select quantiles. I think that was my original intention, which I now
see is a bit different to qqnorm.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: qqnorm and ggplot2 (second round)
parts:
Thanks for keeping in touch!

Well… I don't really need this anymore as I realize that I must use
different parameters for the theoretical distribution (meanlog and
sdlog for qlnorm) for each condition which stat_qq won't allow I
guess.

To go deeper in the details, I analyze the distribution of single cell
fluorescence data acquired with a microscope.
So I have several conditions, for each condition several pictures, and
for each picture a few hundreds of cells.

I want to plot the averaged qqplot of experimental distribution
against the fitted lognormal distribution for each condition. In order
to have an idea of the errors for each condition, I decided to build a
qqplot for each picture, and then to average them by condition, so I
end up trying to average qqplots with different numbers of points (as
the number of cells per picture is not fixed) and hence different x
coordinates.

Finally, I decided to first interpolate each distribution using a
fixed number of points, so that I can average them. Actually, this is
this step that was done by specifying the quantile argument stat_qq if
I got it well.

But once again this would work if my distributions for each condition
had the same parameters which is not the case.
If it is really unclear, I can send a minimal example for curiosity.
Best,

Thomas

Once your statistical transformations get beyond a certain level of
complexity, it's much easier to do them outside of ggplot2, so you can
check each step as you do it. It should be pretty easy to do this
sort of transformation with the plyr package.
